name: Quantum Engraving #002 — Thermal Barrier Surge
description:
Confinement of laser energy within a sub-microscopic dielectric oxide layer (SiO2, 1-5 μm). With a thermal conductivity 100 times inferior to bare silicon (1.4 W/m·K vs 148 W/m·K), the thin film acts as an impenetrable thermal barrier, forcing instantaneous superheating and thermal stress buildup until catastrophic mechanical relaxation at the 1900 Kelvin crack threshold (T_crack).

Conceptually derived from Master's Thesis research in Nanophotonics and numerical simulations in COMSOL Multiphysics ('Modeling and implementation of laser engraving considering the impact of layers material', University of Tabriz). This artwork visualizes the step-wise thermal insulation effect and smoothed Heaviside boundary transition (flc2hs).

Note: This artwork is an artistic interpretation inspired by multiphysics simulations and theoretical models; it does not claim to be a raw numerical export.
creator: Alireza Mahdipour Shadkam
